title: Thousand Separator
statement: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return its decimal digits as a string in which a dot (`"."`) separates every group of three digits, counting the groups from the right. The leftmost group may have one, two or three digits; numbers with at most three digits get no dot, and no leading zeros are added.
notes:
## Intuition

Dots belong at fixed distances from the **right** end: before the last 3 digits, the last 6, the last 9, and so on. Reading the digits left to right, a digit needs a dot in front of it exactly when the number of digits from it to the end is a multiple of 3, unless it is the very first digit. (A brute-force alternative peels off `n % 1000` repeatedly, but must zero-pad the inner groups.)

## Approach

1. Turn `n` into its decimal string `digits`.
2. Walk the positions `i` from left to right, with `remaining` digits from `i` to the end.
3. If `i > 0` and `remaining` is a multiple of 3, append a dot to `result`.
4. Append `digits[i]`, and return `result` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 987`, so `digits = "987"`. At `i = 0`, `remaining = 3`, but this is the first digit, so no dot: `result = "9"`. At `i = 1`, `remaining = 2`: `"98"`. At `i = 2`, `remaining = 1`: `"987"`. No dot was added, so the answer is `"987"`. (For `1234`, `remaining = 3` at `i = 1` puts the dot after the `1`: `"1.234"`.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(d), where d is the number of digits (at most 10).
- Space: O(d) for the string.

## Pitfalls

- Group from the right, not the left: `1234` is `"1.234"`, not `"123.4"`.
- Never put a dot before the first digit, even when the length is a multiple of 3 (`"987"`, `"123.456"`).
- When building with `% 1000`, groups like `5` in `1005` must be written `"005"`; `n = 0` must still give `"0"`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `digits` | `n` written in decimal |
| `result` | the formatted string built so far |
| `i` | position of the current digit |
| `remaining` | digits from position `i` to the end, inclusive |

narration.2: Work on the decimal digits of n as a string.
narration.3: The answer is built up one character at a time.
narration.5: Visit the digits from left to right.
narration.6: Count the digits from this one to the end, including it.
narration.7: A multiple of 3 means a group of three starts here, unless this is the first digit.
narration.8: Separate the groups with a dot.
narration.12: Every digit is placed; return the formatted string.
